The ResNet34, PointNet2Stage, IEF/IMNet networks and ray/PCL AABB CUDA kernels are copied from the official implementation. The surrounding full-image pseudo-depth pipeline is implemented separately in model.py. This is an adaptation of official stage one, not a bit-for-bit reproduction of the original RGB-D training/inference pipeline. It does not include the original RefineNet stage.

## Preserved learned architecture and geometric definitions

- ResNet34 output stride 8, input RGB channels 3, output channels 32; no ImageNet pretrained weights, matching the upstream Resnet34_8s constructor.
- PointNet2Stage input dimension 6 (relative metric XYZ followed by RGB), output dimension 128, base width 32. The RGB values sent to PointNet are the same ImageNet-standardized RGB values as those sent to the ResNet, not raw 0..255 or unstandardized 0..1 colors.
- Eight position frequencies and four ray-direction frequencies; absolute ray entry/exit position encodings. Decoder input dimension 385.
- IEF offset decoder with two updates, width 64; IMNet termination decoder with width 64. Both retain upstream use_sigmoid=False and the original soft-clamping activation.
- RGB ROI boxes extend four pixels in each direction, are clamped to the image, and use ROIAlign output size 2x2, spatial_scale=1 and aligned=True, exactly as upstream pipeline.py.
- Unit camera rays originate at the camera center. Offset distance is the predicted scalar times sqrt(3) times voxel side length. Per-ray termination classification uses scatter log-softmax; position selection takes the detached raw-score maximum, mathematically equivalent to the softmax maximum before finite-precision rounding.
- The fixed base metric volume is [-1,-1,0] to [1,1,2] metres, expanded by half a voxel on every face. At the registered resolution 8, voxel side is .25m and the expanded bounds are [-1.125,-1.125,-.125] to [1.125,1.125,2.125]. The volume is never enlarged using GT or input extrema.
- Occupied cells and point-to-cell associations follow upstream batch_get_occupied_idx with overlap=False. Each image is processed separately instead of including batch IDs in one large cell list. Default-resolution cell bounds, point IDs and inverse indices are checked against the actual upstream function; relative coordinates can differ by float32 rounding because subtraction is reassociated.
- Position, termination and surface-normal loss weights remain 100, .5 and 10. Surface normals retain the forward horizontal/vertical differences, cross product, normalization epsilon 1e-8, and half cosine distance.

## Explicit pseudo-depth adaptation differences

1. Validation and deployment inputs are RGB, calibrated K and frozen V2-plus-learned-Laplacian E08 metric Z-depth. Training uses an explicit 20/20/20-epoch curriculum: valid GT background transitions from weight 1 to 0, while transparent or invalid-GT pixels always retain frozen predicted depth. Training GT segmentation determines the mixture region, never the query set or a model input channel. GT background therefore DOES affect training support points and occupied cells; no GT or sensor depth/mask affects validation or deployment inputs. No transparent holes are carved.
2. Support validity means finite positive predicted depth; selected points outside the fixed volume are excluded. Training chooses up to 10,000 support pixels by uniform random selection from valid raster indices. Evaluation uses deterministic uniformly spaced valid raster indices, independent of rank, batch order and epoch. Upstream instead uses randomized sampling in 8x8 block order and repeats points when fewer than the requested count exist; this adaptation uses the available points without repetition.
3. Evaluation queries every pixel. Training samples at most 20,000 raster indices using a uniformly selected start and a circular contiguous interval. Every pixel has equal direct-query probability; the non-circular interval in the earlier adaptation had a vertical sampling bias. Normal stencils still use real image neighbors, with last-row/column exclusion; circular query indexing does not join opposite image boundaries. GT masks do not select queries. Query chunks bound temporary matrices; geometry is processed per image and RGB features per minibatch.
4. Input depth, GT depth and query rays all use the same calibrated K at the current image resolution and integer pixel-center coordinates. XYZ is constructed after resizing depth with the corresponding transformed K. The data layer explicitly accounts for pixel-center resize conventions; upstream resizes precomputed XYZ and scales principal points directly. Therefore the whole resize/unprojection pipeline is intentionally not a bitwise copy.
5. Forward inference can omit GT entirely. GT membership and loss construction are conditional. In eval mode, providing arbitrary GT changes diagnostics/losses only, never the predicted depth. Training epochs 0..5 use a GT-positive termination cell when one exists. If no positive candidate exists, they use the learned termination choice; upstream can select an arbitrary all-zero-label candidate in this case. From epoch 6 onward and in all evaluation, selection uses learned scores.
6. Queries with no intersecting cell, empty support, or nonfinite/nonpositive predictions retain the supplied depth: the curriculum mixture during training, and pure frozen V2/E08 depth during validation/deployment. Upstream uses a zero-position sentinel for no-intersection queries. Invalid input is sanitized to zero and reported. Registered predicted-depth caches require finite positive values. Fallback queries remain in position-loss and evaluation denominators; the frozen input has zero position gradient.
7. Position supervision excludes nonfinite/nonpositive GT and any externally supplied invalid-GT pixels, whereas upstream position L1 does not explicitly mask zero GT. Empty valid-GT or positive-termination sets contribute a differentiable zero instead of NaN. Every parameter is connected to a zero term, including empty-support batches and empty probability labels, so DDP receives zero gradients rather than unused parameters.
8. Training normal loss fills unsampled neighbors with GT, following upstream's supervised loss construction. This temporary image is never a model input. Normal supervision additionally requires valid GT at the current, right and lower pixels; it excludes the last row/column and degenerate GT normals (normalized norm <= .5). Upstream averages all queried normal terms without these validity guards. Normal loss is computed from the final depth including explicit V2 fallback; original failure/zero-sentinel behavior is not retained.
9. Intersection coverage, valid prediction coverage, actual replaced fraction, fallback reasons and training-only GT-cell coverage are reported. These diagnostics never use GT to choose inference fallback. Evaluation metrics and validation-only checkpoint selection are handled outside the model, rather than by the original pipeline's mandatory compute_loss call and test-set validation loop.
10. Nonfinite-loss/gradient handling, frozen first-stage caching, calibrated-camera provenance, full-image and transparent-region baselines, and experimental split selection are integration responsibilities documented by the containing project. The original training dataset mixing, input corruptions, and RGB/depth noise augmentation are not implicitly applied by these vendored network modules.

## Runtime compatibility changes

- Imports use this package's namespace; an unused upstream training-utility import is replaced by a minimal weight-loading helper. The registered training path uses no pretrained checkpoint and never invokes that helper.
- Global autograd anomaly detection is removed. The IEF initial offset is registered as a non-learned device-moving buffer; this adds offset_dec.init_offset to the state dictionary, with no additional trainable parameters.
- CUDA sources are resolved relative to model.py, not the process working directory. Kernel launches use PyTorch's current stream and check launch errors. Geometric kernels remain float32/int32. Automatic mixed precision is disabled inside the stage-one wrapper.
- The containing distributed trainer converts BatchNorm to SyncBatchNorm before wrapping with DDP, matching the original distributed training setup. Inference uses evaluation mode and fixed support selection.
- A graph-connected zero through RGB features keeps SyncBatchNorm backward collectives connected on empty-support ranks, inheriting the independently verified 2026-10-27 OracleBackground fix.
- Candidate selection uses the raw detached score maximum and integer scatter-min of pair indices to break exact ties deterministically. This avoids distinct logits rounding to equal float32 softmax probabilities and changing the chosen cell across query chunk sizes. Teacher-positive candidates use the same deterministic tie rule; classification loss is unchanged. Pre-fix traces and regression results are retained in the experiment audit directory; no claim is made that this alone explains historical experiment degradation.

## Verification scope

tests/test_model.py optionally loads the actual upstream network class definitions from LIDF_OFFICIAL_SOURCE (default /home/hengxianli/LIDF) on CPU. It checks identical learned state-dictionary names/shapes, trainable parameter count, and bit-exact seeded parameter initialization; the only extra state entry is the IEF offset buffer. This establishes learned-network topology/initialization equivalence, not end-to-end pipeline equivalence. tests/test_geometry.py separately checks default-resolution voxel assignment against the actual upstream voxelization function, including boundary and nonfinite points. Other tests exercise GT-free prediction, GT independence in evaluation, query-chunk parity, finite backwards with missing labels, and full V2 fallback with zero parameter gradients.
